name: Luís Fontes
bio: I've been writing code for more than 20 years, and at some point that passion for building things became an obsession with making them secure — across web apps, smart contracts, and everything in between. I still code constantly, still find new ways to harden systems, and still haven't run out of side projects. This blog is where both worlds collide.

projects.name: OrgSec Guide
projects.description: A comprehensive checklist and guide for organizations looking to implement a robust cybersecurity program.

projects.name: XXExploiter
projects.description: Tool to help exploit XXE vulnerabilities. Generates XML payloads and automatically starts a server to serve DTDs or perform data exfiltration.

projects.name: VSCode Swissknife
projects.description: Scriptable VS Code extension to generate or manipulate data. Stop pasting sensitive data into webpages.

projects.name: DamnVulnerableCryptoApp
projects.description: An app with intentionally insecure crypto. Perfect for testing and exploiting weak cryptographic implementations and learning crypto without diving deep into the math.

projects.name: Watchtower
projects.description: VS Code extension that scans your workspace for malicious configurations, invisible Unicode threats, and dangerous IDE attack vectors — fully local, fully open source.

projects.name: Warden
projects.description: Enforce file-based policies on managed machines by automatically detecting and correcting config files that drift from approved values.

projects.name: Coup Sheet
projects.description: If you like the board game Coup as much as I do, you'll find this sheet super helpful.

projects.name: MirageVM
projects.description: JavaScript virtual machine for code obfuscation. Protects sensitive client-side logic with custom bytecode through a low-level language that supports all JavaScript features. (Private project)

projects.name: How To Test Secrets
projects.description: A visual, interactive cheat-sheet for testing whether leaked API keys and secrets are still valid — pick a service and get a ready-to-run command.

projects.name: hash-identifier-js
projects.description: JavaScript port of hash-identifier. Identifies the hashing algorithm used to generate any supplied hash value.
